A desktop that feels like yours

Everything in its place.
Exactly where you put it.

Keep the things you open every day close. Give everything else a place to belong.

A place for everything.

Four tile sizes. Movable groups. Folders that expand in place. Pin an app, a document, a directory or a shortcut, then drag things into a layout that makes sense to you.

A translucent preview follows your pointer. Select several tiles to move them together, edit with the keyboard, undo a move, or lock the layout against accidental changes.

Less looking. More doing.

Press the Windows key and type. Find an app, supported Windows settings, or indexed local filenames. The selected result is ready for Enter.

Windows-key integration and local file search are optional. You decide what belongs in Start.

Make room for your colors.

Follow your Windows theme or choose light or dark. Explore five color families, set your own accent and background colors, use your desktop wallpaper, or choose a separate image just for Start.

High contrast and reduced motion follow your Windows accessibility settings.

More than shortcuts

A little life
on your desktop.

Time, focus, PC activity, your chosen photos, weather and headlines. Nineteen included tiles turn a launcher into a glanceable part of your day.

A workspace for your ideas

Small canvas.
Make something yours.

Build a clock, a dashboard, a reading corner or something no one has tried yet. Ordinary HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Four tile sizes. A preview for each.

Start with one of nineteen editable examples. Use SVG, Canvas, responsive CSS and transparent backgrounds. Highlighted source, Tab indentation and offline formatting help you keep the code readable.

Test click actions before pinning. Hide live tile names when your design needs the whole surface. News stories scroll inside their tile; neighboring tiles stay put.

A few useful answers

Before you
make yourself at home.

Do I need to install anything else?

The portable ZIP includes its .NET dependencies. HTML live tiles and Tile Studio previews require Microsoft WebView2 Runtime. Live tile setup guide.

Does it replace Explorer?

ReStart runs as an independent app. Its optional Windows-key and taskbar Start-button integrations are reversible. It does not patch Explorer or inject a DLL.

Does it upload my app list?

No advertising or usage analytics are included. Your app list, layouts and photo-folder selections are not uploaded. If you enable a tile connection, its provider receives the requests and parameters you choose. Read the security policy.

How is the first layout chosen?

ReStart chooses familiar installed apps by role, using app identities and exact translated names. Missing apps are replaced with offline bundled tiles, giving each initial group at least six tiles. Existing layouts stay yours; this also applies when you explicitly reset the layout. How initial layouts work.

What about multiple monitors and accessibility?

Native window-placement checks cover two displays at 100%/125%/150% scaling, including mixed portrait/landscape. Accessibility providers are checked in all eight languages and both themes; basic Narrator announcements were inspected through Speech recap. Display reconnects, physical touch and full screen-reader interaction still need device checks. See the measured coverage.

Can I use my own language?

ReStart supports English, German, Spanish, French, Japanese, Korean, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese. Translations are AI-assisted; corrections are welcome.

How do I update?

ReStart can check public GitHub Releases and notify you at startup when an update is available. The startup check is optional. Download the new ZIP and replace the complete extracted package after closing the app. Local settings stay separate from the app folder. Update guide.

Is it made by Microsoft?

No. ReStart is an independent, MIT-licensed project inspired by the late Windows 10 full-screen Start menu. Windows and the illustrated app names are trademarks of their respective owners.
